thread.title_full: Grief and fury as thousands gather at vigils for Annunciation Church victims - NewsBreak

author: Adam Uren
title: Grief and fury as thousands gather at vigils for Annunciation Church victims - NewsBreak
text:
By Adam Uren ,
13 minutes ago
Thousands gathered to grieve the traumatic events in Minneapolis on Wednesday, which saw two children killed and 17 injured in a mass shooting at Annunciation Church and Catholic School.
Vigils were held Wednesday evening in a packed gymnasium at the Academy of Holy Angels in Richfield, and then at Lynnhurst Park in south Minneapolis, a short distance from the church and school where Robin Westman opened fire, killing an 8-year-old and a 10-year-old and injuring 14 children and three adults.
The emotional scenes at both vigils, with tears shed among many of the mourners, were accompanied by calls for action from the political leaders who spoke at the events, and called for swift and significant action on gun control, with some calling for an assault rifle ban.
"Don't come to me with thoughts and prayers and you won't talk about a ban on assault rifles," said Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison, referring to the common refrain of "thoughts and prayers" often expressed in the event of school by those who later oppose any form of gun restrictions.
"It's not about the right to bear arms to these people; it's about the right to sell arms."
Bring Me The News
View the 5 images of this gallery on the original article Among those speaking at the Lynnhurst vigil in addition to Ellison were Mayor Jacob Frey, Rep. Ilhan Omar, Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, Rep. Angie Craig, Sen. Amy Klobuchar, local city council members Emily Koski and Linea Palmisano, and State Sen. Zaynab Mohamed.
Frey was among those critical of the proliferation of guns in America, telling those in attendance not to think of the victims on Wednesday as somebody else's kids but as your own.
"Think about the last thing you told you son or daughter when you said goodbye to them this morning. The gentle kiss on the cheek, a few kind words, shoving them a pack of apple sauce, you should be able to do that with the confidence that you're going to see them again that evening," he said.
"You should be able to do that because our schools, our system, our society can keep these kids safe, because these beautiful children at Annunciation should not be going through this right now, they should be learning math and playing at recess, and messing around at cafeteria, and playing with their friends, that's what childhood is about.
"But what we know is that far too often people are robbed of this childhood because of this senseless gun violence. And don't let anyone tell you that it's not about guns because it is."
Lt. Gov. Flanagan said: "God weeps, Jesus weeps in this moment because we have free will and we have been given all of the tools necessary to stop this violence against our children.
"If we have the courage and if we watch people continue to come year after year after year to the Capitol to demand more, you must continue coming to the Capitol, you must continue raising your voices, you must continue to pray and to turn that prayer into action."
